---
title: "Retail Customer & Basket Analysis"
---

End-to-end customer and product analytics on a synthetic retail transaction dataset, demonstrating five techniques in both R and Python — from classic market basket analysis to modern probabilistic CLV modeling.

## Chapters

1. [Association Rules](01-association.qmd) — market basket analysis with `arules` (R) and `mlxtend` (Python), side by side.
2. [BCG-style Clustering](02-cluster-2d-bcg.qmd) — products positioned by market share × growth (Python / scikit-learn).
3. [RFM Clustering](03-cluster-3d-rfm.qmd) — articles segmented by Recency, Frequency, Monetary value (R / kmeans + interactive 3D with plotly).
4. [Customer Lifetime Value](04-clv-bgnbd.qmd) — probabilistic CLV with BG/NBD + Gamma-Gamma (Python / `lifetimes`).
5. [Survival Analysis](06-survival.qmd) — Kaplan-Meier and Cox PH on time-to-first-repeat (Python / `lifelines`).
6. [Demand Forecasting](07-forecasting.qmd) — monthly revenue per product group with naive, ETS and SARIMA baselines (Python / `statsmodels`).
7. [Product Embeddings](08-embeddings.qmd) — co-occurrence × PPMI × SVD for substitution lookup and semantic clustering (Python / scikit-learn).
8. [Causal Uplift](09-causal-uplift.qmd) — meta-learner CATE estimation: did the discount cause the repeat purchase? (Python / scikit-learn).
9. [Insights](05-insights.qmd) — synthesis of the upstream chapters with cross-cuts and headline recommendations.

Plus a [**dashboard view**](dashboard.html) of the same findings, and a standalone [Python notebook](notebooks/rfm_clustering.ipynb) that replays the RFM analysis in Colab.

## Data overview

The dataset is synthesized to mirror a two-year transaction log from a furniture / home-goods retailer.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Rows** | ~6,400 line items |
| **Transactions** | ~3,500 baskets |
| **Customers** | 2,400 (heavy-tailed transaction count, BG/NBD-shaped) |
| **Articles** | 66 SKUs across 40 distinct product names |
| **Date range** | 2015-07-01 to 2017-06-30 |
| **Categories** | 10 (dining, living, bedroom, office, lighting, electronics, decor, storage, kitchen, outdoor) |

The synthesis encodes co-purchase patterns (e.g. *dining_table → dining_chair* at 85%), temporal trends (some articles grow over the window, others decline), and customer-level structure (lifetime + transaction rate per customer, BG/NBD-style). Full schema and design rationale: [`docs/DATA_SPEC.md`](docs/DATA_SPEC.md).

For methods we considered and deferred (survival analysis, demand forecasting, prod2vec, causal uplift), see [`docs/ROADMAP.md`](docs/ROADMAP.md).

## Reproducing locally

```bash
# Generate the deterministic synthetic dataset (seed=42)
python scripts/generate_synthetic_data.py

# Render the site
quarto render
quarto preview          # auto-reload during editing
```
